'''Jacqueline Ficini''' (October 20, 1923 – December 7, 1988)<ref name="1FRWP">{{cite web |title=Moteur de recherche des décès |url=https://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/index2.php?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdeces.matchid.io%2Fid%2F0TYHjLvB1a6H#federation=archive.wikiwix.com&tab=url |website=deces.matchid.io |via=wikiwix.com |access-date=14 February 2026}}</ref> was a French researcher and professor of chemistry. While her research addressed various fields of [[organic chemistry]], she is remembered in particular for initiating and developing the synthetic chemistry of ynamines.{{efn|The ynamines are a particularly unstable subclass of synthetic alkynes.<ref name="DeKorver2010">{{cite web |last1=DeKorver |first1=Kyle A. |last2=Li |first2=Hongyan |last3=Lohse |first3=Andrew G. |last4=Hayashi |first4=Ryuji |last5=Lu |first5=Zhenjie |last6=Zhang |first6=Yu |last7=Hsung |first7=Richard P. |title=Ynamides: a modern functional group for the new millennium |url=https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2927719/ |website=Chemical Reviews |access-date=14 February 2026 |pages=5064–5106 |doi=10.1021/cr100003s |date=8 September 2010}}</ref>}} She was appointed a full professor at the [[University of Paris VI]] in 1965 where she spervised multiple doctorate theses. She also headed a laboratory consisting of six [[CNRS]] researchers and eight assistant professors.<ref name="2FRWP" /> 
 
In early 2026 it was announced that Ficini was one of the 72 women to have their names added to the [[List of the 72 names on the Eiffel Tower|Eiffel Tower to join the 72 men]] already included.

==Early life and education==
'''Jacqueline Jeanne Ficini''' was born on October 20, 1923 in [[Saint-Maixent-l'École]], a commune in the French department of [[Deux-Sèvres]]. She was the daughter of Jane Pontet and her father was Colonel Raoul Ficini.<ref name="2FRWP">{{cite book |language=fr |first=Jean-Pïerre |last=Genet |chapter=Jacqueline Ficini (19231988) |title=European Women in Chemistry |publisher= John Wiley & Sons |editor-first1=Jan |editor-last1=Apotheker |editor-first2=Livia |editor-last2=Simon Sarkadi |year=2011 |isbn=9783527636464 |doi=10.1002/9783527636457.ch49 }}</ref><ref name="3FRWP">{{cite book |editor1-last=Lafitte |editor1-first=J. |editor-first2=Stephen |editor-last2=Taylor |chapter=Ficini (Jacqueline, Jeanne) Universitaire |title=Who's who in France, Paris |year=1988 |url=https://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/index2.php?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.google.fr%2Fbooks%2Fedition%2FWho_s_who_in_France_Paris%2FpicMAQAAMAAJ%3Fhl%3Dfr%26gbpv%3D0%26bsq%3DJacqueline%2520Ficini%25201988#federation=archive.wikiwix.com&tab=url |access-date=14 February 2026}}</ref>

She studied at the Collège Saint-Marie de Chavagne in [[Angoulême]] and then attended the universities of Paris and [[Angers]] to complete her master's degree. Also at the [[University of Angers]], in 1952, she obtained a doctorate in [[physical sciences]] under the supervision of R. Rothstein.<ref name="2FRWP" /><ref name="3FRWP" />

== Career ==

=== Academic appointments ===
Following her doctorate, she began her career as a research assistant at [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] in 1952 until her appointment as an instructor in chemistry at the Faculty of Sciences at the [[University of Paris]] in 1957.<ref name="2FRWP" /> She then went to the United States for a postdoctoral fellowship, which she completed at [[Columbia University]] in 1960 with G. Stork as research associate. In 1962, she returned to France as a lecturer (first maître assistant, later maître de conférences) at the Faculty of Sciences at [[University of Reims Champagne-Ardenne]]. She was promoted to full professor at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University|University of Paris VI]] in 1965 where she assumed various responsibilities and headed the doctoral school of organic chemistry.<ref name="2FRWP" /><ref name="3FRWP" /> From 1964 to 1988, she supervised 18 state doctoral theses (doctorats d'état) and 26 engineer theses (thèses de docteur-ingénieur). She headed a laboratory consisting of six CNRS researchers and eight assistant professors.<ref name="2FRWP" />

=== Research ===
As a researcher, in 1956 in collaboration with Professor Henri Normant, she first became interested in investigating [[Organometallic chemistry|organometallic compounds]] and the reactivity of [[Grignard reagent]]s. With Professor Gilbert Stork, in 1961 she developed catalysts stemming from her innovative [[Metal-catalyzed cyclopropanations|intramolecular cyclization]] of an unsaturated diazocarbonyl compound. While at Paris VI, she experimented with functionalized vinyl halides and alkyl lithium to develop a [[lithium-halogen exchange]]. Her most notable achievement was however her development of ynamines chemistry, demonstrating their rapid reaction with alcohols to produce O, N-acetals. Her work covered the formation of amides known as the Ficini-Claisen rearrangement, complementing the [[Claisen rearrangement|Eschenmoser rearrangement]].<ref name="2FRWP" />

Specializing in the field of ynanime chemistry, Ficini was elected president of the Organic Chemistry Division of the [[Société chimique de France|French Chemical Society]].<ref name="2FRWP" /> The importance of the Ficini-Claisen rearrangement using chiral ynamides has recently been recognized, several decades after Ficini's death. In particular, the chemistry of ynamines has led to growing interest in ynamides.<ref name="2FRWP" />

During her career, Ficini spoke as an invited guest as some 130 conferences in France and internationally. She published over 120 articles, reviews and patents.<ref name="2FRWP" />

=== Affiliations ===
Ficini was elected president of the Organic Chemistry Division of the [[Société chimique de France]].<ref name="2FRWP" /> She was also a member of the [[American Chemical Society]] and was an invited professor of New York's [[Columbia University]] in 1975, 1978 and 1985.<ref name="2FRWP" /><ref name="3FRWP" />

=== Death ===
She was invited to Japan by Professor Yoshida in 1988. Upon her return to France, she died in Paris on December 7, 1988, aged 65.<ref name="2FRWP" /><ref name="5FRWP">{{cite journal |title=We regret to report the death of Prof. Jacqueline Ficini |journal=Chemistry International |year=1989 |url=https://www.google.fr/books/edition/Chemistry_International/3CJFAQAAIAAJ?hl=fr&gbpv=0&bsq=Jacqueline%20Ficini |access-date=14 February 2026 |publisher=Pergamon Press |language=en |volume=11 |page=87 }}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
* Le Bel Prize (1972) from the French Chemical Society for her contribution to ynamine chemistry<ref name="3FRWP" /><ref name="2FRWP" />
* [[Jecker Prize]] (1979) for her work on functional vinyllithia and ynamines<ref name="6FRWP">{{cite news |title=La tour Eiffel va honorer pour la postérité 72 femmes de science |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/sciences/article/2026/01/26/la-tour-eiffel-va-honorer-pour-la-posterite-72-femmes-de-science_6664180_1650684.html |access-date=14 February 2026 |date=26 January 2026 |language=fr |trans-title=The Eiffel Tower will honor 72 women scientists for posterity}}</ref>
* Berthelot Vermeil Medal (1979)<ref name="6FRWP" />
* Academic Palms (1974) for services to education<ref name="2FRWP"/>
* Knight of the [[Legion of Honour]] (1986)<ref name="2FRWP" />
In 2026, Jacqueline Ficini is among the 72 pioneering women scientists whose names have been proposed to be added to the commemorative frieze on the first floor of the [[Eiffel Tower]], where only men's names have appeared until now. The plan was announced by the Mayor of Paris, [[Anne Hidalgo]] following the recommendations of a committee led by [[Isabelle Vauglin]] of ''Femmes et Sciences'' and Jean-François Martins, representing the operating company which runs the Eiffel Tower.<ref name="7FRWP">{{cite news |last1=Jacquin |first1=Jean-Baptiste |title=La tour Eiffel va honorer pour la postérité 72 femmes de science |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/sciences/article/2026/01/26/la-tour-eiffel-va-honorer-pour-la-posterite-72-femmes-de-science_6664180_1650684.html |access-date=14 February 2026 |date=26 January 2026 |language=fr |trans-title=The Eiffel Tower will honor 72 women scientists for posterity}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Les noms des 72 femmes pour la Tour Eiffel ont été révélés. |url=https://www.femmesetsciences.fr/news/les-noms-des-72-femmes-pour-la-tour-eiffel-ont-%C3%A9t%C3%A9-r%C3%A9v%C3%A9l%C3%A9 |access-date=2026-03-23 |website=Femmes & Sciences |language=fr}}</ref><ref>[https://10ca8303-b3dc-4a91-9dcc-2d2b91792b47.usrfiles.com/ugd/10ca83_3838bd19a41a4e83927cfc8fe0f50404.pdf 72 femmes de sciences pour la tour Eiffel] ''Femmes & Sciences'' (in French). Retrieved 2026-03-23</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Eiffel Tower: a list of 72 women scientists will soon be inscribed on the Parisian monument |url=https://www.sortiraparis.com/en/news/in-paris/articles/340564-eiffel-tower-list-of-72-women-scientists-soon-to-be-honored-on-the-paris-landmark |access-date=2026-03-23 |website=www.sortiraparis.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-01-26 |title=Eiffel Tower to honor 72 women scientists for posterity |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/france/article/2026/01/26/eiffel-tower-to-honor-72-women-in-science-for-posterity_6749828_7.html |access-date=2026-03-23 |language=en}}</ref>

== Selected publications ==
In addition to her many papers, Ficini published several books:<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.idref.fr/02686441X|title=Ficini, Jacqueline (1923-1988)|publisher=IdRef|access-date=3 July 2026|language=French}}</ref>

*(1952) Sur l'ouverture des époxydes primaires-secondaires et primaires-tertiaires par l'ester malonique sodé<ref>{{cite book |last=Ficini |first=Jacqueline |year=1952 |title=Sur l'ouverture des époxydes primaires-secondaires et primaires-tertiaires par l'ester malonique sodé|publisher=Université de Paris |location=Paris |oclc=45193819 |page=86 |url= |access-date=|language=French}}</ref> (University thesis)

*(1974)  Structures de la matière cinétique chimique, éléments de chimie physique <ref>{{cite book |last=Ficini |first=Jacqueline |date=1 January 1977 |title=Structures de la matière cinétique chimique, éléments de chimie physique 
|publisher=Pergamon Press |location= |isbn=978-2705658427 |page=193 |url= |access-date=}}</ref>

*(1976)  Ynamine: A Versatile Tool in Organic Synthesis (Tetrahedron Report)<ref>{{cite book |last=Ficini |first=Jacqueline |date=1 September 1976 |title= Ynamine: A Versatile Tool in Organic Synthesis (Tetrahedron Report)|publisher=Pergamon Press |location= |isbn=978-0080204666 |page=38 |url= |access-date=}}</ref>

*(1977) Thermodynamique: Équilibres chimiques (Eléments de chimie-physique)<ref>{{cite book |last=Ficini |first=Jacqueline |date=1 January 1977 |title=Thermodynamique: Équilibres chimiques (Eléments de chimie-physique)  |publisher=Hermann |location=Paris |isbn=978-2705658489 |page=188 |url= |access-date=|language=French}}</ref>
